headline: 76.5% of toothpaste samples contain microplastics, Bangladesh study finds
summary: A recent study conducted in Bangladesh has revealed a significant presence of microplastics in a majority of toothpaste brands tested.
details: A study in Bangladesh has found that 76.5% of toothpaste samples tested contain microplastics. This discovery highlights a widespread issue with plastic contamination in common personal care products.

Microplastics are tiny plastic particles that can enter the human body through ingestion or inhalation. Their presence in toothpaste means these particles could be entering the body during daily oral hygiene routines.
The research emphasizes the need for stricter regulations and better monitoring of ingredients used in consumer products to protect public health and the environment.
Environmental experts warn that these microplastics eventually wash into water systems, contributing to the long-term pollution of oceans and rivers.
caption:

The research emphasizes the need for stricter regulations and better monitoring of ingredients used in consumer products to protect public health and the environment.

Environmental experts warn that these microplastics eventually wash into water systems, contributing to the long-term pollution of oceans and rivers.

headline_marked: CEC [[to meet Speaker on presidential election schedule]]
headline: CEC to meet Speaker on presidential election schedule
summary: Chief Election Commissioner A M M Nasir Uddin will consult with Acting Speaker Kaisar Kamal to finalize the dates for the upcoming presidential election.
details: Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) A M M Nasir Uddin is set to meet with Acting Speaker Kaisar Kamal to discuss the schedule for the presidential election.
Election Commission Senior Secretary Akhtar Ahmed announced the on Sunday during a press briefing at the Election Building.
The CEC's office held an unscheduled meeting on Sunday with all election commissioners and the senior secretary to review the laws governing presidential elections.
According to protocol, the CEC must meet the Speaker before announcing the election schedule. Following this meeting, the next steps for the announcement will be determined.
The presidential election is conducted via a vote by Members of Parliament. The Parliament Secretariat will send the voter list of MPs to the EC Secretariat for finalization.
The process follows the resignation of Md. Sahabuddin on Friday afternoon. Acting Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmed has assumed the role of Acting President.
Under the current constitutional provisions, a new president must be elected within 90 days of the vacancy of the office.
caption:
A new president for Bangladesh is on the horizon. The Election Commission is moving to finalize the schedule.

Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) A M M Nasir Uddin is set to meet with Acting Speaker Kaisar Kamal to discuss the schedule for the presidential election.

Election Commission Senior Secretary Akhtar Ahmed announced the on Sunday during a press briefing at the Election Building.

The CEC's office held an unscheduled meeting on Sunday with all election commissioners and the senior secretary to review the laws governing presidential elections.

According to protocol, the CEC must meet the Speaker before announcing the election schedule. Following this meeting, the next steps for the announcement will be determined.

The presidential election is conducted via a vote by Members of Parliament. The Parliament Secretariat will send the voter list of MPs to the EC Secretariat for finalization.

The process follows the resignation of Md. Sahabuddin on Friday afternoon. Acting Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmed has assumed the role of Acting President.

Under the current constitutional provisions, a new president must be elected within 90 days of the vacancy of the office.
